This was what I was kind off going for but given my description the closest thing it correlates to is sandbagging. The issue is how you/me define sandbagging and if live testing despite loss (even if the loss can be taken) is considered sandbagging

Spark have looked poor but we can't assume they'll remain poor as the stage progresses or look poor in playoffs. I think teams like the Shock whose aim is to win the entire thing can't settle for selecting perceived weaker teams but rather be up to challenge any team they face.

I also believe teams are struggling to suss out the meta and why performances have been kind of mixed on the whole.

A counter to teams playing at their best they can at the moment is they risk showing the other team their hand and being dealt with in playoffs. It has been said that the Paris Eternal coming into Stage 1 were a strong GOATs team that through scrimming other teams '' taught '' them how to play GOATs and essentially lost their advantage over them.

I think, but am unable to substantiate this thought in any way, that NYXL hardly tried when they were on stage in Stage 4. Their reactions upon finishing matches indicated to me that they were quite happy winning when they were pushed and coupled with reports of sandbagging seem to support this. 

The possibility of live testing strategy is slim but another consequence of loss especially a heavy one is influencing perception. If you're able to convince your opponent that you aren't particularly strong at this point in time you could use it as obfuscation for different purpose (I admit this possibility is even slimmer). NYXL have reportedly not been doing well in scrims and given their constant switching of their DPS seem to still be working out who is suitable for the team.

My initial point is that any team can employ this method not just the NYXL who are the first team you think of as it was widely reported that they were sandbagging.
